title: HCLTech Profit Jumps 21% as Revenue Narrowly Misses Estimates; Forecast Floor Raised
excerpt: Revenue of Rs 35,620 crore came in just under the LSEG consensus, but profit beat, deal wins hit $3.26 billion, and HCLTech narrowed its full-year growth range to 2.5%–4%.
body:
• HCLTech's September-quarter revenue rose 11.5% to Rs 35,620 crore, marginally below the Rs 35,686 crore average LSEG estimate, as clients held back tech spending.
  • Net profit beat expectations, rising 21.2% to Rs 5,132 crore against an estimated Rs 4,859 crore; the company declared an interim dividend of Rs 12 per share.
  • HCLTech narrowed its full-year revenue growth forecast to 2.5%–4%, lifting the floor from 1% after new deal wins of $3.26 billion in the quarter.
  • Annualised AI revenue rose to $219 million from $171 million in the June quarter, and headcount grew by 6,450 as fresher hiring stepped up.

HCLTech narrowly missed revenue estimates for the July–September quarter on Monday, as cautious client spending and AI-driven disruption of traditional billing models weighed on India's third-largest software services exporter — even as profit comfortably beat expectations and the company raised the floor of its annual forecast.

Consolidated revenue rose 11.5% year on year to Rs 35,620 crore ($3.72 billion), just below the Rs 35,686 crore average estimate compiled by LSEG, according to Reuters. Net profit rose 21.2% to Rs 5,132 crore, ahead of the Rs 4,859 crore analysts expected. In dollar terms the quarter was HCLTech's slowest September-quarter growth in three years, at about 2.2% year on year — a measure of how flat demand has become across India's $315 billion IT services industry.

The forecast tells the real story

The most closely read number was the guidance. HCLTech narrowed its annual revenue growth forecast to 2.5%–4%, from 1%–4% previously — trimming the top end but, more significantly, raising the floor after a strong bookings quarter. New deal wins totalled $3.26 billion, up from $2.4 billion in the June quarter, taking first-half order wins to a record $5.67 billion. Operating margin came in at 18.2%, up 80 basis points. Most brokerages had expected the forecast to be retained unchanged.

"We saw healthy demand towards the end of the quarter. However, the environment remains fluid."

— C. Vijayakumar, Chief Executive, HCLTech

AI is small, but it is the growth line

Annualised AI revenue rose to $219 million from $171 million in the previous quarter — still a small slice of a $3.72 billion quarter, but the fastest-growing one, as clients prioritise AI, data and operating-model work with a clear efficiency case. The company is also hiring into the shift: headcount rose by 6,450 in the quarter as fresher intake stepped up, according to Moneycontrol's report on the results. An interim dividend of Rs 12 per share was declared.

What to watch

HCLTech's shares slipped in early trade as the market weighed the revenue miss. The sector's reporting season now moves to Infosys, Wipro and Tech Mahindra later this week, which will show whether HCLTech's pattern — profit discipline, soft discretionary demand, AI as the only reliable growth line — is the industry template for the year. For the large Indian tech workforce in the US, the fresher-hiring uptick and the record deal book are the two numbers that matter most: both point to work continuing to flow, even as the work itself changes.
